about: The edc: URI scheme (mappingLayers ML1-a, ruled by BRONZE_CROWN 2026-10-24; respelled in ML3.1 Part A, ruled by AMBER_JOURNEY 2026-10-26: Q41-Q43, Q51). Kinds are DATA: edcUri.js mints and parses only the kinds listed here, and an unlisted kind is refused by name. A template is '/'-separated segments after baseIri; a segment is literal text and {placeholders}. Every placeholder value is encoded by segmentEncoding unless the kind lists it under verbatimPartList (a part copied from an already-minted URI, whose spelling another module owns). The ONE path-valued part (pathValuedPartName) keeps '/' literal: it is encoded piece by piece and joined with '/', must END its template (only an elementPathSuffixTemplateList entry may follow it); that it begins with its standard's CURIE prefix (RULING BR2) is enforced by subjectCurie.js and the exporter, not here (ruled R-1 (a), AMBER_JOURNEY 2026-10-26: measured redundant for disjointness). Every whole-segment literal of every template is a RESERVED WORD that no single-segment placeholder may take as its value; that is what makes the templates disjoint without a lookup. A published URI is never respelled; a scheme change is a new prefix segment (D-URI). Nothing here is published yet (w3id ruled NO public registration; a local stub resolves).

segmentEncoding.about: UTF-8 after NFC; each byte whose ASCII character is in literalCharacterList is kept, every other byte becomes %XX with uppercase hex. '/', '@', '%', space and ',' are therefore always encoded inside a single-segment value; inside the path-valued part '/' separates pieces and every piece is encoded this way (an empty, '.' or '..' piece is refused by forbiddenSegmentTextList).

partPatternByPartName.about: a part listed here must match its pattern at mint and at parse (Q43, Q51: a content hash is 64 lowercase hex, so a label can never pass for one)

listingPaging.about: (ML3.1 Q5) a listing kind answers one page at a time: <listing URI>?<queryParameterName>=N, N an integer from firstPageNumber; absent = the first page; 0, negative, non-integer or past the end is refused by name (no clamping). pageSize is FIXED (no client page size), so a cited page means the same slice for everyone.

vocabularyIriByCurie.about: objects that are vocabulary terms, not graph nodes: an abstention row's object (SSSOM 1.0: sssom:NoTermFound MAY stand as object_id)

vocabularyTermDefinitionByName.about: (ML3-a) what each vocabularyTerm means; the stub resolver returns this text. Raters were never asked a SKOS relation, so neither term claims one; agreement is measured on the object (D-RATERPRED).
vocabularyTermDefinitionByName.bestMatch: The author chose this meaning (HubReference card) as the best answer for the subject element among the cards offered. No SKOS relation (exact, close, broad, narrow) is asserted.
vocabularyTermDefinitionByName.alsoAcceptable: The author marked this meaning as also acceptable (the rater tool's Same) for the subject element, beside a best answer. No SKOS relation is asserted.
vocabularyTermDefinitionByName.cites: (useCaseForge-102926, ruled by SHADOW_MEADOW 2026-10-29) A use case cites an element of another standard, as its author wrote it: the subject is the use case's reference node, the object the cited standard's own node. Asserted by the EDUcore use-case standard; no match (exact, close, broad, narrow) is asserted.
